The Wings for Val Foundation (WingsforVal.org) proudly honors the life and legacy of Lt. Cmdr. Lyndsay Evans (August 21, 1993–October 15, 2024), a Naval aviator whose leadership, discipline, and pursuit of excellence set her apart. Lyndsay represented a generation of aviators who did not wait for opportunity—they created it. She led from the front, held herself to the highest standards, and earned the respect of those around her through consistency, strength, and integrity. This scholarship honors a leader who set the high bar--and met it. Lyndsay Evans did not rely on intention alone. She showed up prepared, took responsibility, and delivered. Her legacy is one of action, accountability, and quiet confidence earned through hard work. This award seeks to recognize a woman who reflects that same standard—someone who is already putting in the work, who understands what it takes to succeed in aviation, and who will continue to raise the bar for herself and others. The goal is not simply to support a pilot in training, but to invest in someone who will lead, by example, in the next generation of aviation.

Through this award, the Wings for Val Foundation seeks to support a pilot in training who will carry forward Val’s legacy with purpose, integrity, and determination—someone who will not only take flight but help shape the future of aviation. These elite bands of women have not only a love of aviation but have put their lives on the line in defense of their country through their military service. WMA is committed to passing this legacy from one generation of women to another and has established an annual scholarship program in support of this commitment. Advocating the love of aviation, WMA offers an annual scholarship to advance a woman in her pursuit of flight ratings at an accredited institution or FAA Approved Part 141 or Part 61 flight school. Applicants must write about their demonstrated persistence and determination to flight. award-1b7e12cc1279.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. The ATP CTP course is a prerequisite for the FAA’s highest certificate. This training program will impart conceptual knowledge through academics and consolidate that knowledge through training in a Flight Simulation Training Device (FSTD). The course bridges the knowledge gap between a pilot who holds a private pilot certificate and a pilot operating in an air carrier environment. This program meets the requirements of FAR §61.156. Successful completion of our FAA-approved course makes you eligible to take the ATP Multi-Engine (ATM) knowledge test, which you may take at any testing center. The ATP Certificate Training Program is 7-9 days long, (32 hours) 4 days ground taught by an experienced airline pilot; (10 hrs) 3 days advanced flight simulation training in a Level D Full Flight Sim; (4 hours) 1 day of Level D Flight Training Device as crew; (6 hrs) 2 days of Level D Full Flight Sim (FFS) as crew. This scholarship does not include lodging and transportation. Training must be scheduled to commence no later than one year from award. Cannot be converted to cash value or transferred to any other course or person.

award-c36fdba14b1f.text: Applicant must be a current WAI member. All applications include a typed 500-word essay. In memory of aviation pioneer Esther Noffke, George J. Priester Aviation is awarding one flight training scholarship worth $5,000. Esther’s passion for aviation was evident from a young age. In March 1944, Esther and 48 of her classmates earned their silver WASP wings, officially becoming Women Airforce Service Pilots (WASP). In December 1944, when George Priester bought Pal-Waukee Airport, she began the role of his administrative assistant. She became an integral part of the development and growth of the Chicago Executive Airport. In 2010, Esther was awarded the Congressional Gold Medal for her service with the WASP. Esther’s legacy in the aviation industry is marked by her unwavering dedication and the significant impact she had on the institutions with which she was associated.
